newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares gain, seen adding on.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares gain, seen adding on.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed 0.3 percent in a technical rebound on Tuesday and traders expect further moderate gains before the end of the week.
"According to latest news Slovenia's chances to join NATO in the first round of its expansion have increased. That may be sufficient to push the index up slightly this week," a trader said.
Membership of NATO and the EU was expected to encourage foreign investors to buy Slovenian securities as the country's credit rating was likely to improve in the event of membership, he added.
In the short-term, market participants said direction hinged upon whether parliament would ratify the agreement with the European Union within the next two weeks.

"When the agreement is ratified shares may jump 10 percent in a matter of days, but if parliament fails to do so shares could fall between 10 to 30 percent," said Goran Brankovic, a trader at Nova Ljubljanska Banka.
* The blue-chip index firmed 0.3 percent to 1,318.89.
* Petrol company Petrol was the most actively traded, up 0.76 percent to 17,330 tolars on volume of 1,848 shares.
